t6642.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Muslim ibn al-Muthannā, also called Ibn Mihrān ibn al-Muthannā, al-Kūfī, the muezzin, trustworthy (thiqah), of the fourth generation; his name is also said to be Mihrān.

t6866.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Muqātil ibn Bashīr al-ʿIjlī al-Kūfī as acceptable, of the sixth generation.
stu: Named next to each other in two or more indexed chains

t7182.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Nufayʿ al-Ṣāʾigh, Abū Rāfiʿ al-Madanī, who settled in Basra. He is described as trustworthy and firmly established, well known by his kunya, and belonging to the second generation.
as: بصري، تابعي، ثقة من كبار التابعين
A Basran Successor, trustworthy, of the senior Successors.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
There is no harm in him.
ابن سعد, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
خرج قديما من المدينة، وهو ثقة
He left Medina early, and he is trustworthy.
al-ʿIjlī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
الطبراني, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
ورجح الطبراني أن اسمه كنيته ووثقه
Al-Ṭabarānī preferred that his kunya is his name and declared him trustworthy.
أبو عمر, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
مشهور من علماء التابعين، أدرك الجاهلية
A well-known scholar among the Successors who lived in the Jāhiliyyah.
وهو مشهور من علماء التابعين، أدرك الجاهلية
He is a well-known scholar among the Successors and lived in the Jāhiliyyah.
He is a well-known scholar among the Successors.

t7308.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Hisham ibn Abi Ya'la, a teacher of al-Thawri, as unknown, from the sixth generation.

t7458.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī al-Makkī as maqbūl, of the sixth generation, marked as a distinguishing identification.

t7524.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith, who transmitted from his brother Zahdam, as weak, of the eighth generation, and whoever confused him made an error.

t7599.bio: Ibn Ḥajar calls Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūhib, al-Taymī al-Madanī, abandoned (matrūk); al-Ḥākim was more severe and accused him of fabricating hadith; of the sixth generation.
as: Al-Ḥākim was even more severe and accused him of fabricating hadith.

t790.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Bayān ibn Bishr al-Muʿallim al-Ṭāʾī as unknown (majhūl), of the sixth generation, noting al-Khaṭīb and Abū al-Faḍl al-Harawī distinguished him from the preceding one.

t7951.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū al-Baddāḥ ibn ʿĀṣim al-Balawī, ally of the Anṣār, trustworthy, of the third generation, who died in 110 AH; those who claimed he was a Companion erred.

t8136.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū Sufyān, client of Ibn Abī Aḥmad, as trustworthy and of the third generation, with his name given as Wahb or Qazmān.

t8392.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Abū al-Mundhir, client of Abū Dharr, as "acceptable" and of the third generation.

t8464.bio: Ibn Ḥasana al-Juhanī: obscure, unnamed, of the third generation; al-Bukhārī cites him.

t8518.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam al-Zuraqī, who transmits from an unnamed man, and in one version from an unnamed Companion.

t8666.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Qaylah bint Makhramah al-'Anbariyyah as a female Companion who has a long hadith.
